tagline: REPLACE: one line under the title: what participants can do after the course
description: Participants go from tensors to a working generative model and learn what each layer of the stack does. For a fictional crafts cooperative they write a training loop by hand, debug a network that will not learn, adapt a pretrained image model to synthetic textile images, implement attention for a toy sequence, build bilingual semantic search with sentence embeddings, and generate text with a small open-weight model while varying sampling settings. They finish by comparing model families on quality, size, latency, licence and cost for three of the cooperative's use cases.
audience: Practitioners. Graduates and early-career developers who have completed the FN courses or passed the placement test, and software engineers moving into AI work.
prerequisites: AE-201 Machine Learning Foundations and Model Evaluation
FN-103 Mathematics for Machine Learning: Vectors, Gradients and Probability
Multiplies matrices and computes a derivative with the chain rule
Has trained and evaluated a model with a train, validation and test split

outcomes.text: Explain how a transformer turns input tokens into next-token probabilities, naming the role of embeddings, attention, the context window and sampling, given an annotated architecture diagram with five blanks and two generated outputs
outcomes.evidence: a completed diagram and a short written explanation scored against a rubric in the supervised check

outcomes.text: Implement a training loop with a loss, an optimiser, mini-batches and validation checks, and use it to train a small network, given a tensor library, synthetic image tensors and a starter script with no training code
outcomes.evidence: a script whose loss and validation curves match the reference behaviour within a stated tolerance

outcomes.text: Apply a debugging checklist to a network whose loss does not fall and correct each fault found, given a training script with three seeded faults in the loss input, the learning rate and data shuffling
outcomes.evidence: a log showing the overfit-one-batch test, each fault and the corrected learning curve

outcomes.text: Use transfer learning to adapt a pretrained image model to a new label set with little data, and measure the improvement over training from scratch, given 800 labelled textile images in eight classes and a laptop CPU time budget
outcomes.evidence: a results table comparing frozen features, partial fine-tuning and training from scratch on the same test set

outcomes.text: Use sentence embeddings to build and test a bilingual semantic search over product descriptions, given 4,000 Arabic and English descriptions and 50 labelled queries
outcomes.evidence: recall at 5 for Arabic, English and mixed queries, with three failure cases and a likely cause for each

outcomes.text: Measure how temperature, nucleus sampling and the instruction change the outputs of a small open-weight language model, given a locally run model and 20 fixed prompts sampled five times each
outcomes.evidence: a table of variation, length and rule violations per setting, with an explanation of one surprising result

outcomes.text: Evaluate model families for three stated use cases on quality, size, latency, licence terms and cost, and recommend one per use case, given a supplied shortlist of open-weight and hosted models and results measured in the labs
outcomes.evidence: a model-choice table with a two-line justification per use case, defended in the capstone

capstone.summary: A small model for one cooperative use case (image classifier, bilingual search or constrained text generation), submitted as a public repository whose README reports training curves, test results, a comparison with a simpler alternative, latency on a laptop and the licence of every model and dataset used, followed by an eight-minute defence and four minutes of questions
